phases.message: Our flights this year were a mess and I want what we're owed. Start here in Tripfold: go through every booking and note the distance, the scheduled arrival and who flew on what fare, for anything that might have been disrupted.
Now my Mailnest travel folder. Find what the airlines wrote about each delay and cancellation: when it was announced, and when we actually got to the gate.
This is Aerolark's claims portal. Check why each Aerolark flight was disrupted and file a claim for every one the rule entitles us to, at the right amount.
And Skyrail's claims portal. Same here, then tell me what you filed and what you left alone, and why.

aerolark_rules.text: Topics: scope, delay, cancellation, extraordinary, amounts, passengers, settlement. One claim per booking. Aerolark pays in cash unless you agree in writing to something else.
Aerolark is an EU airline. Regulation 261/2004 covers every Aerolark flight, wherever it departs from, and every flight of any airline departing from an airport in the EU (Art. 3(1)).

A flight that reaches its final destination three hours or more after its scheduled arrival is compensated as if it were cancelled (CJEU, Sturgeon, C-402/07). Arrival means the moment a door opens at the gate (C-452/13), not the departure delay. Under three hours at arrival: no compensation.

No compensation for a cancellation announced 14 days or more before the scheduled departure (Art. 5(1)(c)). Inside 14 days it is owed, unless Aerolark offered a reroute leaving and arriving close to the original times (within 2 hours before and 4 hours after if told 7 to 14 days ahead; 1 hour before and 2 hours after if told under 7 days ahead).

Not owed when the cause was an extraordinary circumstance that could not have been avoided (Art. 5(3)): weather that closes an airport or stops departures, air traffic control decisions and strikes by air traffic controllers, bird strikes (C-315/15), security alerts. Not extraordinary: technical faults found before departure or in maintenance (C-549/07), crew shortages, and strikes by the airline's own staff (C-28/20).

Per passenger (Art. 7): 250 euros for flights of 1,500 km or less; 400 euros for flights within the EU over 1,500 km and other flights of 1,500 to 3,500 km; 600 euros for all other flights. Distance is great-circle, by the last destination of the booking. On a flight over 3,500 km that arrives between 3 and 4 hours late, Aerolark may halve it (Art. 7(2)); from 4 hours, it is paid in full.

Every passenger with a confirmed booking is covered, including award tickets paid with miles (Art. 3(3)). Passengers travelling free of charge, such as an infant on a parent's lap with no fare, are not covered. State the number of passengers covered on the claim.
Compensation is paid in cash or by bank transfer. A travel voucher replaces it only if you accept it, and accepting an offer made in full and final settlement ends the claim.

aerolark_status.cause: Seasonal schedule change, published 16 May; passengers moved to AL 762 the same day.
Crew shortage at the Lisbon base: no first officer available. Passengers moved to the next day's flight.
Hydraulic leak found on the aircraft at the pre-departure check; replacement aircraft brought from the hangar.
Late inbound aircraft after a cabin pressure fault was repaired in Lisbon.
Thunderstorms: Berlin airport suspended all departures from 16:00 to 18:45 by order of the airport authority.
Faulty fuel quantity indicator replaced before departure.
Strike by Aerolark's pilots, called by the Aerolark pilots' union for 19 and 20 September; flight operated with a reserve crew.
Bird strike on the aircraft's previous landing at Lisbon; mandatory engine inspection before the next flight.

aerolark_offers.terms: In full and final settlement of any claim relating to AL 1432 on 14 August, including under Regulation 261/2004.

skyrail_rules.text: Topics: scope, delay, extraordinary, amounts, passengers. One claim per booking.

Skyrail is a US airline. Regulation 261/2004 covers Skyrail flights departing from an airport in the EU, Iceland, Norway or Switzerland. Skyrail flights into the EU from elsewhere, and flights within or between countries outside the EU, are not covered (Art. 3(1)): ask under the rules of the country of departure instead.

A covered flight that reaches the gate at its final destination three hours or more after its scheduled arrival is compensated (CJEU, Sturgeon, C-402/07). The arrival delay counts, not the departure delay.

Not owed when the cause was extraordinary and could not have been avoided: weather, air traffic control restrictions and strikes by air traffic controllers, bird strikes, security. Technical faults, including a late aircraft held for a repair on its previous flight, are not extraordinary (C-549/07).

Per passenger: 250 euros up to 1,500 km; 400 euros for 1,500 to 3,500 km; 600 euros over 3,500 km. On a flight over 3,500 km that arrives between 3 and 4 hours late, Skyrail may halve it (Art. 7(2)); from 4 hours, it is paid in full.
Every passenger with a confirmed booking is covered, including award tickets paid with Skyrail Rewards miles. Passengers travelling free of charge are not.

skyrail_status.cause: Aircraft change after a brake fault at New York JFK.
Strike by French air traffic controllers: Eurocontrol cut the slots for every flight crossing French airspace.
Late inbound aircraft: its previous flight was held at New York for an unscheduled repair to a bleed-air valve.
Engine sensor fault; spare part flown in from Atlanta.
